rows.figure: Colorado wind, 680 MW at USD 1,400 per kW of 2005: construction jobs, total
rows.quote: Colorado wind [...] During construction period [...] Total Impacts (Direct, Indirect, Induced) 1,618 $58.55 $183.90 (PDF page 11)
rows.why: two releases of the model twelve years apart: the paper ran JEDI II with IMPLAN's 2001 state data and its own Colorado inputs (it prints no local share for wind's equipment); the tool holds the 2018 release of JEDI Wind (2016 state data) at JEDI's default Colorado shares, and scales JEDI's 2017 cost mix to the paper's cost, USD 2,213 per kW in 2025 dollars. The paper does not say enough to split the gap between the two

rows.why: the paper buys 40 percent of the plant's gas from Colorado wells at USD 7 per MMBtu, which JEDI counts as local spending; the tool's default, JEDI's saved share, is 0 percent

rows.figure: construction jobs: the tool's on-site job-years; the order's full-time construction jobs
rows.quote: the Facility would create an estimated 211 full-time construction jobs over the course of construction which would pay an average hourly wage of $60.00 per hour (Director's order, 4 November 2026, page 2)
rows.why: the order counts workers employed, at least 155 in the second quarter of construction; the tool counts job-years of 2,080 hours. The order's Nevada payroll at its wage is 87 job-years (10,857,600 / 60 / 2,080)

rows.figure: construction earnings on site, USD
rows.quote: Construction Payroll in Nevada residents $10,857,600.00 (order, page 4); dollar year not stated, taken as 2025
rows.why: the order counts the payroll of Nevada residents only (at least 50 percent of the construction employees); JEDI's on-site line also holds project development and benefits

rows.figure: operating jobs on site, each year
rows.quote: the Facility would create approximately 0 full-time operational jobs (order, page 2); Operational Payroll in Nevada: $0.00 (page 4)
rows.why: the applicant states no operating employee at the plant; JEDI's 2016 geothermal model staffs every plant

rows.figure: property tax due before abatement, first operating year, USD
rows.quote: Total Taxes Due, First Year After Completion: $ 1,948,119 (Department of Taxation, property tax fiscal note, worksheets of 24 August 2026, page 3)
rows.why: the same base and rate by construction: the rate typed is the note's own (USD 3.1191 per 100 on 35 percent of value); the note's taxable value is USD 178,450,621, the order's investment USD 178,446,043

rows.figure: property tax paid after the 55 percent abatement, first operating year, USD
rows.quote: Total Taxes Available to Local Governments after abatement: $ 876,653 (the same page)
rows.why: the tool's rule for NRS 701A.370 (55 percent abated) gives the Department's figure

rows.figure: property tax due before abatement, 20 years, USD
rows.quote: Total Taxes Due during Period of Abatement (20 years): $ 33,410,592
rows.why: the Department depreciates improvements 1.5 percent a year and personal property by its manual's schedule (taxable value USD 127.6 million in 2048); the tool's value falls in a straight line over the 60 years typed

rows.figure: property tax paid after abatement, the first 20 operating years, USD
rows.quote: Total Taxes Available to Local Governments after abatement: $ 15,034,766 (20 years)
rows.why: the tool counts the abatement's 20 years from the first construction year, so operating years 19 and 20 are taxed in full; the Department abates 20 fiscal years from 2028-29

rows.figure: sales and use tax on the build, USD
rows.ours: not held (JEDI's geothermal model has no sales tax line)
rows.quote: purchase a total of $4,736,195.00 [...] during the first fiscal year [...] $1,184,049.00 [...] during the second year; Sales Tax Rate 6.850% (Department of Taxation, sales and use tax fiscal impact, 19 August 2026): 5,920,244 at 6.85 percent, of which USD 251,610 abated
rows.why: the tool holds no taxable share for geothermal. The two Nevada notes disagree on the base: the Budget Division's note of the same month states purchases subject to the tax of USD 86,426,913, 48 percent of the investment
